questions.q: What determines whether Tableau renders a view as a bar chart versus a line chart, when the fields on the shelves are identical?
options: The mark type selected on the Marks card — switching it to Bar renders bars instead of a line, with no other change to the view
The order fields were dragged onto the shelves
Whether the dataset has more than 100 rows
The color palette chosen for the view
questions.explain: The mark type on the Marks card controls the shape Tableau draws for each data point — Bar, Line, Circle, and so on — independent of the fields themselves.

questions.q: What happens when you drag a second dimension, like Ship Mode, onto Color on the Marks card of a bar chart?
options: Each bar splits into stacked colored segments, one per Ship Mode value, that sum to the bar's original total
The bar chart is replaced entirely with a pie chart
Color has no effect unless the mark type is changed to Square
It removes the dimension already on Rows
questions.explain: Adding a dimension to Color stacks the bar into colored segments — you can still read the bar's overall total while seeing how each segment contributes to it.

questions.q: What does Show Me actually evaluate before suggesting chart types?
options: The fields already in the view or selected in the Data pane, matching them against each chart type's minimum field requirements
The business question the user is trying to answer
The most visually striking chart type available regardless of the data
A random sample of the dataset's values
questions.explain: Show Me only lights up chart types that the currently selected fields can support — it reads field requirements, not intent, so choosing the *right* chart for the question is still up to you.

questions.q: In the Show Me panel, what does hovering over a chart-type icon show you?
options: A description of the minimum field requirements for that chart type
A live preview of every possible chart built from your entire dataset
The exact DAX formula Tableau will generate
A list of every dashboard using that chart type
questions.explain: Hovering over a Show Me icon surfaces the field requirements for that chart type — for example, stacked bars need one measure and one dimension, with an optional second dimension.

questions.q: What does the 'Choose for me' button in Show Me do, and how should you treat it?
options: It automatically picks a chart type from your selected fields — a fast starting point, but every chart it builds should also be one you can build by hand
It permanently locks the view so no other chart type can be selected
It deletes any fields not used by the chosen chart type
It only works after connecting to a live SQL Server connection
questions.explain: Choose for me is a convenient shortcut for picking a reasonable chart type automatically, not a substitute for understanding how to build that same chart manually.
